name: Duck 4
summary: Force motors: the brain sets each joint's force (up to 10 times the standard limits), loose at 0; learning to walk from zero on a flat floor
what_changed: The muscles. Every duck before had position motors, which pull each joint toward the angle the brain asks for like a spring. Duck 4 has force motors (the force_motors body): the brain's command is the force itself, from minus to plus the force limit, with the same limits as Duck 3.3 (10 times the standard). A command of 0 leaves the joint loose. Starting wobble 0.05 (log_std -3.0).
why: Duck 3.3's 10 times stiffer position motors made his legs rigid: asked for 2 m/s he ran about 1.5 m/s, and with free energy about 1.6 m/s, then stopped improving. Francisco wanted muscles that are not stiff but can push hard when the brain wants. The wobble was measured on random moves of a new brain (10 attempts each): with force motors a wobble of 0.05 costs 1.3 J per step, less than the standard duck's start (2.8 J at 0.37), so energy should not make falling on purpose pay, the trap Duck 3.3 fell into at first.
starts_from: Nothing: a new brain, since old brains send angles, not forces
notes: Exam and walking scores can be compared with the walking ducks in flat_walking. With no commands the duck collapses in about 0.4 s, so he has to learn to hold himself up first.

world_settings.name: flat_walking
world_settings.description: Flat floor, walking speeds 0.2 to 0.7 m/s
world_settings.notes: Duck 1, Duck 2 and Duck 2.1. They trained under an older forward reward, without the overshoot rule (going faster than asked did not lose points); this world has today's rule.

body_settings.name: force_motors
body_settings.description: Force motors with 10 times the standard force limits: the brain sets each joint's force, loose at 0
body_settings.notes: Duck 4. The same strength as ten_times_stronger (Duck 3.3), but with no spring: Duck 3.3's 10 times stiffer position motors made his legs rigid, and asked for 2 m/s he ran about 1.5 to 1.6 m/s. Here the brain's command is the force itself, so a leg is as stiff or as loose as the brain makes it.
